hook.line: Tomás has called a meeting at the café about Altamira, and he has no idea who will turn up. Spanish has a neat way to talk about "whoever" and "wherever" before you know the answer.
hook.es: El que quiera venir, que venga.
hook.en: Whoever wants to come can come.

examples.es: El que quiera venir, que venga.
examples.en: Whoever wants to come can come.

examples.es: Quien quiera hablar conmigo sabe dónde estoy.
examples.en: Whoever wants to talk to me knows where I am.
Eat whatever you like. (to a friend)
I'll talk to whoever you want.

rule:
When you don't know yet who, what or where, Spanish puts the verb after *el que*, *quien*, *lo que* or *donde* in a different form, the one that says "whoever it may be".

*quiera* (not *quiere*), *digas* (not *dices*), *sea* (not *es*).

With *tú* the verb ends in *-as*: *quieras*, *digas*. With *él*, *ella* or *usted* it ends in *-a*: *quiera*, *diga*.

If the answer is already known, the normal form comes back: *Hago lo que puedo.* (I do what I can, a real, known thing.)

English just adds "-ever" to the word and keeps the verb. Spanish keeps the word and changes the verb.
smallPrint: Teachers call these *relativas libres* with the subjunctive: a relative clause with no fixed person or thing behind it.

options: Where do you say you're going?

readAndPick.es: Quien quiera hablar conmigo sabe dónde estoy.
options: Whoever wants to talk to me knows where I am.
The one who talked to me knows where I was.
Nobody wants to talk to me.
I talked to the one you wanted.
I talk to the one you want.
I'll talk to whoever you want.

readAndPick.es: Los que quieran quedarse pueden quedarse.
options: Whoever wants to stay can stay.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *quieras* or *quieres*. You don't know yet which dish your friend will pick: Come lo que ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: You can't name the dish yet, so the verb takes the *whoever it may be* form: *quieras*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *sea* or *es*. Whatever it takes, I'll do it: Haré lo que ___ necesario. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: "Whatever is necessary" is not fixed yet, so *sea*.

yourTurn.prompt: I'll go wherever you say. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Donde* plus *digas*: the place isn't decided yet.

yourTurn.prompt: Whoever wants to come can come.
yourTurn.answer: El que quiera venir, que venga.
yourTurn.why: *El que* or *quien* plus *quiera*: anyone, nobody in particular.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Vale instead of you: Voy donde tú digas. Say: I'll go wherever Vale says.
yourTurn.why: Vale is *ella*, so the ending is *-a*: *diga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: Hablaré con quien tú quieras. Say: We'll talk to whoever you want. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Only the first verb changes to *we*; the *whoever* verb still follows *tú*.

yourTurn.prompt: I do what I can. (a real, known thing)
yourTurn.why: The thing is known, so there is no *whoever* form: the normal *puedo*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. When the thing isn't fixed yet, *es* becomes *sea*.
*Quieres* says you already know which dish; for "whatever you like" use *quieras*.

pitfalls.wrong: El que quiere venir, que venga.
pitfalls.right: El que quiera venir, que venga.
pitfalls.why: Anyone at all may come, so the first verb takes the *whoever* form too.
English only needs "-ever"; in Spanish the verb after *quien* is what changes.

personal: Finish the thought about yourself: *Haré lo que sea necesario por…* or *Voy donde tú digas, pero…*
